identity.description: Regime-switching model over a time series: a hidden first-order Markov chain selects which of k regimes' regression/AR parameters (and optionally variance) generates each observation. The product is the smoothed regime-probability path plus per-regime coefficients — 'which era is this series in, and how do its dynamics differ'.

consumes.note: a single regular time-indexed series; the regime chain lives over its time steps
optional exogenous regressors aligned to the series index (MarkovRegression exog)

emits.note: smoothed marginal regime probabilities per time step — the primary product
most-likely regime path (argmax of smoothed probabilities)
k x k regime transition probabilities; expected regime duration = 1/(1-p_ii)
per-regime regression/AR coefficients (and variances when switching_variance) — the 'how the eras differ' story

k_regimes.note: regime count — selected by AIC/BIC; identifiability degrades fast beyond 3-4 regimes on business-length series

switching_variance.note: let the innovation variance switch with the regime — the volatility-regime axis

search_reps.note: random start-parameter draws — the hedge against the multimodal likelihood that makes deterministicFit false

invariances.why: a linear-Gaussian model of the series is equivariant to rescaling — coefficients and variances rescale with it, regime path unchanged
a log transform changes which shifts look like mean-regimes vs variance-regimes — a modeling choice, not a no-op
the Hamilton filter requires a regular, gap-free series; missing periods must be interpolated first
numeric series + numeric exog design columns only
assumes Gaussian innovations within regime, constant within-regime parameters, and first-order Markov regime dynamics
each regime's parameters are estimated only from the time spent IN that regime — a rare regime visited briefly is unidentifiable regardless of total series length
regime-probability-weighted forecasts extend beyond the sample, though the family's product is the regime path, not the forecast

featureStats.why: rolling mean/variance shift statistics are the prior evidence that multiple regimes exist at all; a break-free series makes k_regimes>1 an overfit
large variance ratios across windows are the specific signal for switching_variance=true rather than mean-switching alone
series length divided by k_regimes bounds the per-regime effective sample; too low makes per-regime coefficients unidentifiable — a gate to k=2

modelMetrics.why: likelihood rises with every added regime; the information-criterion penalty on k^2 transition + per-regime params is the honest regime-count selector
expected duration 1/(1-p_ii) — regimes lasting one or two steps are noise labels, not eras; persistence is what makes the regime path meaningful
mean max smoothed probability measures regime separation — values near 1/k mean the filter cannot tell the regimes apart

edgeCases.condition: multimodal likelihood — different start params reach different fits
label switching across refits (regime indices permute)
edgeCases.note: canonicalize regime order by regime mean (then variance) before persisting

edgeCases.condition: k_regimes too high for the series
edgeCases.behavior: transition probs pinned to 0/1, degenerate regimes

edgeCases.condition: using smoothed regime probabilities as an as-of feature
edgeCases.behavior: smoothed probs use the FULL series (future leakage); only filtered_marginal_probabilities are as-of-safe

driver.constructor: MarkovRegression(endog, k_regimes, trend, exog, switching_variance).fit(search_reps=...) / MarkovAutoregression(endog, k_regimes, order, ...).fit(search_reps=...)
driver.wrapperNeeds: series adapter (time_col, value_col, freq); expose smoothed_marginal_probabilities as latent-state and its argmax as state-sequence; canonical regime reordering for stable labels across refits

canBeSeeds.via: latent-state -> features:tabular adapter (current-regime probability as a feature)

placementClaims.why: the Hamilton filter needs a gap-free regular series; time-aware interpolation, not tabular median
a log transform stabilizes multiplicative variance so mean-regimes and variance-regimes are not conflated
scale-equivariant — standardization changes nothing about the regime path or fit quality
single numeric series; exogenous design columns are a modeling concern, not preprocessing
